conflicts.description: Real-time inventory sync vs. daily batch sync for product information from SAP — two requirements specify conflicting sync strategies for SAP data.

version_a.text: Inventory levels must sync with SAP in real time to prevent overselling.

version_b.text: Product information must sync from SAP via batch process once daily.

conflicts.description: Vendor pricing control vs. central admin pricing control — vendors are given a portal to manage product information, but a business rule explicitly prohibits vendors from setting prices, while US-016 implies vendors manage their listings (which typically includes pricing).

version_a.text: Vendors cannot set product prices; only central admin controls all pricing.

version_b.text: The system shall allow vendors to create, update, and manage their product listings.

conflicts.description: Vendor pricing control vs. central admin pricing control — TR-008 states vendors manage their own product listings via dedicated login, implying full listing management including price, while TR-021 prohibits vendors from setting prices.

version_a.text: Vendor partners manage their own product listings and inventory via dedicated login.

version_b.text: Vendors cannot set product prices; only central admin controls all pricing.

conflicts.description: Data localization constraint requiring servers physically in India conflicts with GDPR compliance, which is a European regulation with its own data residency and processing requirements that may conflict with strict India-only storage.

version_a.text: All customer data must be stored on servers physically located within India.

version_b.text: Platform must comply with GDPR regulations for NRI customer data handling.

conflicts.description: SAP as system of record with real-time sync conflicts with batch daily sync — TR-050 mandates SAP as the authoritative source requiring up-to-date data, while TR-028 allows product information to be stale by up to 24 hours via batch.

version_a.text: Platform must use SAP as the system of record for product and inventory data.

version_b.text: Product information must sync from SAP via batch process once daily.

conflicts.description: Admin manages products and pricing per TR-007 and US-014, but TR-026/TR-050 designate SAP as the system of record for product data, creating a conflict over who or what is the authoritative source for product and pricing updates.

version_a.text: The system shall allow central admin to set and update product prices and discounts.

version_b.text: Platform must use SAP as the system of record for product and inventory data.

conflicts.description: Admin manages and adds products per US-013, but SAP is the system of record per TR-050 and TR-026 — it is contradictory whether products are created/managed in the platform or in SAP and synced.

version_a.text: The system shall allow central admin to add, edit, and deactivate products in the catalog.

version_b.text: System must integrate with SAP ERP to migrate and sync product data.

conflicts.description: Peak load assumption may be underestimated — TR-049 flags that the 50,000 concurrent user figure may underestimate online traffic, directly contradicting the sufficiency of TR-040 as a performance requirement.

version_a.text: Platform must handle at least 50,000 concurrent users during peak sale events.

version_b.text: 50,000 peak users is based on physical store footfall and may underestimate online traffic.

conflicts.description: TR-053 requires a marketing tool or integration for email/SMS campaigns, while TR-045 requires the system itself to support sending promotional emails and SMS — these conflict on whether the capability is native or via integration.

version_a.text: System must support sending promotional emails and SMS to customers.

version_b.text: System must support a marketing tool or integration for email and SMS campaigns.
